description: Shared view objects the AppView's XRPC methods return. These describe the AppView's canonical DOMAIN entities as served over the wire (the reconciled internal shapes), NOT the public atproto repo records (com.example.wiki.post / .comment / .reaction / .resolution), which are a separate, publish-time shape. Field names are snake_case to match the served JSON. The NSID is a placeholder pending a minted namespace.

authorView.description: An author: either a resolved account (a DID) or a free-text name with no account (the census found ~42% of author chips are free-text). Exactly one of `did`/`display` is present, discriminated by `kind`.

kind.description: `user` when the author is a resolved account, `free_text` otherwise.

did.description: The author's DID (present only when `kind` is `user`; during migration this may hold the interim user id until DID binding).

display.description: The free-text author name (present only when `kind` is `free_text`).

documentView.description: A content node: document / folder / file / proposal, with its authors and its place in the tree.

kind.description: The content sub-kind (open set: unknown values are tolerated for forward compatibility).

slug.description: The URL segment, unique among live siblings. The server picks it from the name.

path.description: The slugs from the root, slash-joined: what the URL carries, and what resolveNode takes.

parent_id.description: The parent node, a context or a document. Absent for a root.

attachable.description: Whether children may be added (the folder lock).

owner_did.description: Who created it. Distinct from authorship.

deleted_at.description: Set while the node is in the bin. No read but the bin's own serves such a node.

deleted_root.description: The node whose deletion took this one to the bin: itself, or an ancestor.

mutable.description: Whether it may still be edited. Submitting a motion clears it.

data.description: What the node holds beside its text: a file's id and type, a cover image. An object, or absent.

content.description: The Slate document JSON, carried verbatim (parsed only at the publish seam). Absent for content-free nodes (folders).

authors.description: Zero or more authors (the census found up to 8 per node), each a DID or a free-text fallback.

visibility.description: `public` content is mirrored to a repo; `private` stays AppView-only.

published_uri.description: The at-uri of the mirrored public record, when published.

legacy_id.description: The interim node id this row was migrated from (import provenance).

contextView.description: A context: a group, an event or a site, the org's organizing structure, with its place in the tree.

slug.description: The URL segment, unique among live siblings. The server picks it from the name.

path.description: The slugs from the root, slash-joined: what the URL carries, and what resolveNode takes.

parent_id.description: The parent node, a context or a document. Absent for a root.

attachable.description: Whether children may be added (the folder lock).

owner_did.description: Who created it. Distinct from authorship.

deleted_at.description: Set while the node is in the bin. No read but the bin's own serves such a node.

deleted_root.description: The node whose deletion took this one to the bin: itself, or an ancestor.

commentView.description: An internal threaded comment on a document or another comment.

on_id.description: The document or comment this replies to.

reactionView.description: An emoji reaction to a subject, addressed by the subject's at-uri.

id.description: The reaction record's at-uri (its primary key).

subject_uri.description: The at-uri of the record being reacted to.

reactor_did.description: The reactor's DID (absent only for a not-yet-realized user).

userView.description: A person. The DID is the identity; the rest is profile, absent until it has been read from their PDS.
